title: Nvidia weighs Perplexity investment at $30B-plus valuation as revenue hits $750M
subtitle: The Information reports Nvidia is in early talks to join Perplexity's next round at a valuation more than 50% above last year's $20B mark, with the AI search startup's annualized revenue tripling since January.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia is in early discussions to invest in Perplexity's next equity financing round at a valuation of more than $30 billion, The Information reported on August 24, with Reuters and Bloomberg confirming the talks. The round would mark a more-than-50% jump from Perplexity's roughly $20 billion valuation a year ago. Nvidia is already an investor alongside Jeff Bezos, SoftBank, Accel, and NEA — the company has raised more than $1.7 billion to date. Terms, including the size of Nvidia's potential check, have not been disclosed, and neither company has confirmed the talks. CEO Aravind Srinivas has publicly targeted a 2028 IPO regardless of when OpenAI or Anthropic list.

The number that matters is on the top line: Perplexity's annualized revenue has climbed above $750 million, up from under $250 million at the start of 2026 — roughly a tripling in eight months. Much of that growth is attributed to Perplexity Computer, the company's cloud-based AI agent that automates browser and desktop tasks for professional users. A $30 billion mark on $750 million ARR pencils to a 40x revenue multiple, which is aggressive but in line with what AI infrastructure adjacent companies are commanding this cycle.

The pattern here is one Nvidia has been running all year. The chipmaker is repeatedly writing checks into companies that consume Nvidia GPUs — Poolside got $7 billion three days ago, OpenAI has a $100B-plus infrastructure partnership, CoreWeave, xAI, and Mistral all took Nvidia capital. Analysts have started calling it the compute-landlord strategy: use the balance sheet to seed demand for the silicon. The Perplexity check would extend that thesis from foundation-model developers into the application layer, right as Google's AI Mode has started squeezing traditional search referral traffic.

A note for learners: watch the multiple, not just the headline valuation. A 40x forward revenue multiple assumes the growth curve holds — that Perplexity Computer keeps compounding, that enterprise seats convert, and that Google doesn't out-execute in the same lane. If any of those slip, the multiple compresses fast. The lesson generalizes: in a market where every AI company gets called a rocket ship, the honest number is always revenue growth divided by valuation growth. If valuation is climbing faster than revenue, someone is paying for a story.
